phaseAuthority: Slide 7 delivery order; slides 3–4 proposed science alternatives
scope: Mission phase extension only; Rev09 mass and geometry unchanged; no Aeolus source incorporation

phases.title: 01 Rideshare
phases.description: Show FREYA carried by the host second stage, then capsule separation. Cold-gas hardware remains on the detachable reentry module.

phases.title: 02 Orient
phases.description: Acquire the burn attitude with optical/MEMS estimation and cold-gas control, then start vehicle telemetry.

phases.title: 03 Deorbit
phases.description: Perform the retrograde burn, confirm its completion and detach the expendable reentry module.

phases.title: 04 Entry
phases.description: The heat shield, aerodynamic shape and low center of gravity support passive entry and deceleration. Do not credit cold-gas control after module jettison.

phases.title: 05 Carrier extraction
phases.description: Remove the cover, deploy the carrier parachute, extract the carrier and discard the aeroshell. Begin the independent carrier telemetry sequence.

phases.title: 06 Probe release
phases.description: Descend to the release gate. Release every probe individually, deploying its own smaller parachute for descent and stabilization.

phases.title: 07 Probe delivery
phases.description: Show nose-first impact and schematic emplacement for every probe. Activate instruments and telemetry using the antenna integrated with retained parachute shrouds.

phases.title: 08 Science operations
phases.description: Acquire soil, run blanks and controls, apply the selected proposed protocol, and inspect detector readout and interpretation. The two source protocols remain alternatives.

phases.title: 09 Data return
phases.source: Presentation slide 7 · probe telemetry; Rev09 SYS-001 and COM-01–05
phases.description: Buffer science and engineering records, repeat the carrier status word, and illustrate an assumed orbiter relay and onward return to Earth.

gas-trap.name: Slide 4 · sealed gas and trap assay
gas-trap.sample: 0.25 cm³ per vessel; proposed 2–5 cm source depth
gas-trap.conditions: No water added; sealed and dark at −10 to 0 °C for 1–5 sols
steps: Soil into test and control vessels
Illustrate acquiring soil from the proposed 2–5 cm source zone and loading 0.25 cm³ into each vessel. This does not demonstrate sample acquisition.
Show no-soil controls and baseline counts, O₂ and pressure before dosing; keep controls distinct from the test vessel.
Illustrate separate ³H₂ and ¹⁴CO test channels and a defined time-zero count. No physical dosing or radioactive hardware is controlled.
Show a compressed incubation review segment: no water added, dark, −10 to 0 °C, 1–5 sols proposed. Playback seconds are not incubation time.
Show gas counting and transfer to cold-water/CO₂ trap detectors. Counts identify retained label; they do not identify a molecule or prove biology.
Illustrate the accounting question for label absent from gas and traps. Leaks and sorption remain alternative explanations; extraction would be needed to identify larger products.
Show test/control comparison and valid non-detection checks. A difference can motivate further investigation; it does not establish life.

extract.name: Slide 3 · incubation and extraction concept
extract.sample: Approximately 1 g soil; sample provenance and controls required
extract.conditions: Near Mars ambient pressure; proposed 0–5 °C incubation
steps: Illustrate approximately 1 g soil alongside heat-treated, no-soil and known-microbe control concepts. These are proposed validation steps.
Record baseline detector and environmental observations and keep controls separate from the unmodified test sample.
Illustrate candidate ¹⁴CO₂, ¹⁴CO, ³H₂ or ³H₂O channels. These are alternative experimental inputs, not a selected flight recipe.
Illustrate near-ambient-pressure incubation at 0–5 °C. Do not merge this temperature or water assumption into the slide 4 gas/trap concept.
Illustrate excess-gas removal, carbonate-control acidification and water-soluble versus oil-soluble extraction concepts. Hardware and sample transfer remain unverified.
Show detector acquisition for retained label in separate fractions, with sensitivity and interference still requiring laboratory validation.
Compare test/control and hydrophobic/hydrophilic behavior. Abiotic incorporation, chemical interference and contamination must be considered before any biological interpretation.
